To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel method for mutation prediction in liquid biopsy samples, and that our method can detect somatic cancer mutations in VAFs that is 2-3 orders of magnitude lower compared with the state-of-the-art methods.
we have developed a new method for somatic mutation detection that can detect mutations at very low VAFs, and that this method is applicable to cfDNA plasma.

we developed a deep learning based mutation calling method for liquid biopsy, which enables detection of mutations in VAFs that is independent of the depth, and that is applicable to both simulated and real clinical samples, and that is able to detect mutations at VAF as low as 0.001%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new machine learning methods for mutation prediction, and the application of these methods to the early detection of cancer using liquid biopsy methods.
the development of a new computational method for the analysis of sequencing data, and with its application to a novel diagnostic application.
the development of new methods for the detection of somatic cancer mutations in liquid biopsy, and in particular the ability to detect mutations at ultra-low variant frequencies.

we developed a deep learning method for the prediction of cancer mutations in ultra-low variant allele fractions (VAFs).

the proposed method is the first method to enable the detection of cancer-associated mutations in cfDNA plasma at VAFs of 10x-3 and 10x-5, and that the proposed method enables the detection cancer mutations in cfDNA at VAFs 2-3 orders of magnitude below state-of-the-art methods, and that the method has been validated on both simulated and clinical samples.
the method described in this paper is able to identify somatic mutations in plasma cfDNA at very low VAFs, and that the results are validated in both simulated data and in clinical samples.

deep learning can be applied to the detection of cancer-associated mutations in cfDNA.
